optimizer_wording_verified_directly.extracted_text_paraphrase: The shared optimiser is Adam with learning rate 10^-3 and weight decay 10^-4; batch size 512; every model trained for 25 epochs.
optimizer_wording_verified_directly.other_mentions: PDF p.19 (Section 7.1): 'Adam at learning rate 10^-3' for ablation configurations.
optimizer_wording_verified_directly.conclusion: The paper names Adam and gives a weight-decay value. It does not say AdamW, decoupled decay, or L2-in-gradient, so AdamW is not established as the paper's optimizer and is not equivalent to Adam with weight_decay.

documentation_vs_code_findings_for_later: configs/milestone1_paper_described.json, protocol and REPORT say domain clipping is per-feature [min_train, max_train]; research/paper_described_baseline.py clamps to scalar [0,1] and the PGD random start does clamp(x+noise, x-eps, x+eps) then [0,1] with torch.manual_seed(seed*10000+batch_idx) per batch (config says torch seeded with training seed).
FGSM/PGD clamp to [0,1] after epsilon clamp or vice versa inconsistently for clean inputs outside [0,1] (validation has 2 out-of-range values; the report states test is within [0,1]).

config training.optimizer_type_evidence claims plain Adam + weight_decay is 'mathematically equivalent for Adam but not the decoupled form' and calls AdamW 'more principled'; README/REPORT say AdamW was 'chosen for correct decoupled decay'. Paper says only 'Adam with ... weight decay'.
